extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for naming inventors, contents and execution of inventor oaths/declarations (and substitute statements), identification of inventors in various application types (provisional, nonprovisional, international), and procedures for correcting inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide inventor names or a unique alphanumeric identifier when inventor unknown (37 CFR 1.41(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is filed without an application data sheet or an inventor’s oath/declaration, or when a provisional application is filed without a cover sheet, the name and residence of each person believed to be an actual inventor should be provided when the application papers pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (c) are filed. Where no inventor(s) is known and applicant cannot name a person believed to be an inventor on filing, the Office requests that an alphanumeric identifier be submitted for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identifiers that are specific, alphanumeric characters of reasonable length; avoid very short identifiers to prevent confusion. Present the identifier clearly so processing personnel can find it. Failure to supply at least a unique identifying name or identifier may result in inability or delay in matching subsequently submitted papers and could require resubmission of time‑sensitive papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for international applications entering national stage (37 CFR 1.41(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of an international application entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 is the inventor(s) set forth in the application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 filed with the initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may change U.S. inventorship at national stage entry by filing an application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 with the initial 371 submission. 37 CFR 1.41(e) does not permit naming the inventor(s) via the inventor’s oath or declaration in lieu of an application data sheet when an ADS is not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for international design applications (37 CFR 1.41(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an international design application designating the United States, inventorship is the creator(s) set forth in the international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correction of inventorship in such international design applications must be made pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional inventorship determination (pre‑AIA rule 37 CFR 1.41(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the inventorship of a nonprovisional application is the inventorship set forth in the oath or declaration as prescribed by § 1.63, except as provided in §§ 1.53(d)(4) and 1.63(d). If no oath/declaration is filed during pendency, inventorship is that set forth in the application papers filed pursuant to § 1.53(b), unless applicant files a paper (with processing fee) supplying or changing the inventor name(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a first-filed executed oath or declaration sets forth a different inventive entity than initially provided at filing, the executed oath/declaration will determine actual inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional inventorship determination (pre‑AIA rule 37 CFR 1.41(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of a provisional application is the inventorship set forth in the cover sheet as prescribed by § 1.51(c)(1). If a cover sheet is not filed during pendency, inventorship is that set forth in the application papers filed pursuant to § 1.53(c), unless applicant files a paper (with processing fee) supplying or changing the inventor name(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the cover sheet to establish inventorship for provisional applications; absent it, the application papers filed under § 1.53(c) determine inventorship unless superseded by a formal submission with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When names/residence/citizenship should be provided if oath/cover sheet absent (pre‑AIA and post‑AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: In nonprovisional or provisional applications filed without the prescribed oath/declaration or cover sheet, the name, residence, and citizenship (where applicable) of each person believed to be an actual inventor should be provided when the application papers pursuant to § 1.53(b) or § 1.53(c) are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying these bibliographic data at the earliest opportunity enables Office identification of the application and prevents mismatches of subsequently filed papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship (37 CFR 1.48 / MPEP §602.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship in an application is permitted by amendment under 35 U.S.C. 116, implemented by 37 CFR 1.48. Requests to correct inventorship filed on or after September 16, 2012 are treated by the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is granted, OPAP will correct Office records and send a corrected filing receipt. See MPEP §602.01(c)(1) and (2) for procedures for requests under different subsections and for requests to correct/update inventor names or change name order; 1.48 requests filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 will be handled by OPAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of inventor's oath or declaration (35 U.S.C. 115 and 37 CFR 1.63(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor’s oath or declaration must identify the inventor(s) by legal name, identify the application, include a statement that the person believes themselves to be an original inventor or joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application, and state that the application was made or was authorized to be made by the person executing the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, unless supplied in an ADS, the oath/declaration must identify each inventor's mailing address and residence (37 CFR 1.63(b)). The signer must have reviewed and understand the contents of the application and be aware of the duty to disclose material information under 37 CFR 1.56 (37 CFR 1.63(c)). There is no minimum age, but the person must be competent to execute the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement in lieu of oath or declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(d) & 37 CFR 1.64 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of executing an oath or declaration, the applicant may provide a substitute statement under permitted circumstances for any individual who is (A) deceased, (B) under legal incapacity, (C) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, or (D) is under an obligation to assign but refuses to make the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute statement must identify the individual, set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis, and contain any additional information or showing required by the Director. The substitute statement must be signed by the applicant (not the unavailable inventor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing oath/declaration, substitute statement, or recorded assignment (35 U.S.C. 115(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall provide each required oath or declaration, substitute statement, or recorded assignment meeting statutory requirements no later than the date on which the issue fee for the patent is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although filing by issue fee date is allowed, earlier filing avoids prosecution complications. See exceptions for earlier-filed application copies in 35 U.S.C. 115(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier‑filed application exception for required statements (35 U.S.C. 115(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for executing oaths, substitute statements, or recorded assignments do not apply to an individual with respect to a later application claiming benefit of an earlier-filed application if an acceptable oath/declaration, substitute statement, or assignment was executed and filed in the earlier-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding this exception, the Director may require that a copy of the executed oath/declaration, substitute statement, or assignment filed in the earlier-filed application be included in the later-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; ability to withdraw/replace/correct (35 U.S.C. 115(h) & 37 CFR 1.63(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a statement under 35 U.S.C. 115 may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time. If changes in naming inventors require additional statements, the Director shall establish regulations to permit such additional filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may not thereafter require an individual who has already executed a compliant oath/declaration or assignment to make additional equivalent statements in connection with the application or any patent issuing thereon. A patent shall not be invalid or unenforceable based on failure to comply if the failure is remedied as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of penalties required in declarations/statements (35 U.S.C. 115(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 115 must contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement made therein is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 by fine or imprisonment of not more than 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oaths/declarations include this acknowledgment either by signature in accordance with 37 CFR 1.66 or by an explicit acknowledgement under the signature provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment may serve as oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment may serve as the oath or declaration required by 37 CFR 1.63 if (i) the assignment includes the information and statements required under 37 CFR 1.63(a) and (b), and (ii) a copy of the assignment is recorded as provided in 37 CFR part 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use a conspicuous indication (e.g., check-box on assignment cover sheet) when an assignment is submitted both for recording and to serve as the inventor’s oath/declaration. Note process differences: paper-filed assignments are forwarded for recordation after assignment of application number; electronic filings via USPTO PES will be made of record in the application but not forwarded to the Assignment Recordation Branch for recordation. Recording of assignments must be done electronically via EPAS; if submitted via EPAS with the check-box, a copy will be placed in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution/signature requirements for oaths/declarations (37 CFR 1.63(g) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must be executed (signed) in accordance with 37 CFR 1.66 or include an acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001. For substitute statements under 37 CFR 1.64 the substitute is signed by the applicant; for assignment-statements the inventor under obligation of assignment must sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple joint inventors exist, the collective oaths/declarations/substitute statements executed by or with respect to all joint inventors meet the chapter I requirements unless otherwise clear in context. See MPEP §602.08(b) for additional details on execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity and application identification requirements in oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63 and MPEP §602.08 references)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must identify the inventor(s) by legal name and identify the application to which it is directed. Unless supplied in an ADS, it must identify mailing address and residence (if different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are necessary to ensure compliance with 35 U.S.C. 115(a) and to enable the Office to identify the application. See MPEP §602.08(c) for the minimum information necessary to identify the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously executed oaths/declarations in continuing applications (37 CFR 1.63(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration or substitute statement is not required in a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) if (i) an oath/declaration was executed in the earlier application, (ii) the continuation/divisional was filed by all or fewer inventors named in the prior application, (iii) the spec/drawings contain no new matter, and (iv) a copy of the executed oath/declaration from the prior application showing signature or indication of execution is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ADS is not filed before or concurrently with the copy of the earlier oath/declaration, the inventorship of the continuing application is the inventorship set forth in the copy of the earlier oath/declaration unless accompanied by a §1.33(b) signed statement naming each inventor in the continuing application. Any new joint inventor named in the continuing application must provide a compliant oath/declaration (except per §1.64). Additional documentation required where prior application was accorded status under §1.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and checklist guidance (PTO forms and quick reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms PTO/AIA/01 through PTO/AIA/11 may be used for submitting inventor’s oaths/declarations in applications filed on or after September 16, 2012; an 'AIA Inventor's Oath or Declaration Quick Reference Guide' is available on the USPTO website. For applications filed before September 16, 2012, Forms PTO/SB/01 through PTO/SB/04 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and guides are available at www.uspto.gov/PatentForms (or corresponding legacy forms pages). An unsigned ADS will be treated only as a transmittal letter; ADS must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA oath/declaration extra contents and foreign priority disclosure (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(b)(2)/(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑AIA oaths/declarations had to state that the person reviewed and understands the application contents and acknowledged duty to disclose (37 CFR 1.63(b)(2)/(b)(3)). They also had to recite all foreign applications for which priority is claimed, including application number, country, and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre‑AIA filings, include full foreign priority information unless supplied on an ADS. See MPEP §602.03 for defective oaths/declarations guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction/update of inventor names or order under 37 CFR 1.48(f) (post‑Sept 16, 2012 handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests filed on or after September 16, 2012 under 37 CFR 1.48(f) to correct or update inventor names or to change the order of inventor names will be handled by OPAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §602.01(c)(2) for the procedures and note that 1.48 requests filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP regardless of application filing date.
